title: Total Recall: Agent Memory and Harness Engineering — Ignacio Martinez, Oracle
talk_summary: The talk frames an agent as a frozen model plus a harness and walks through harness layers: storage/memory, retrieval, semantic layer, agent loop, and context engineering.

takeaways.what_they_do: They store available tools and skills in a retrievable catalog and inject only the relevant ones into the context window per agent-loop iteration.

takeaways.technique: Hybrid short-term files plus long-term database memory
takeaways.what_they_do: They keep ephemeral working state in files and promote durable facts, preferences, and memories into a structured database with search.
takeaways.evidence_quote: short-term memory, right? That lives in files. And when something needs to be promoted into a long-term memory

takeaways.technique: One git worktree per concurrent agent
takeaways.what_they_do: When multiple agents edit files, each works in a separate worktree and merges after implementation to avoid file-level races.
takeaways.evidence_quote: after the implementation is done, they will merge to master, or the merge to main, sorry.

takeaways.what_they_do: They set a patience/hysteresis limit on tool calls before giving up, and route hard problems to frontier models while easy ones can use smaller models.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I found that a value of 8 to 12, like maximum number of tool calls before giving up, is correct.
takeaways.numbers: 8-12 max tool calls before giving up

takeaways.evidence_quote: The topics will orient the model. The summary will compact the thread and it will state the current intent

takeaways.what_they_do: After a successful complex workflow, they distill it into an improved skill file, retire the old version, and reuse the new one.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can promote it through a distillation process and create a better skill.md than the original
